prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a refined design study for CLEAN TUNER, showing THREE matching portrait app screens side by side on a warm neutral presentation canvas. High resolution landscape composition. Reference image is ONLY a reference for warm frosted champagne silver materials, softly recessed warm ivory glass and beautifully precise subtle bevels. Completely redesign the meter and remove the old controls. Contemporary premium analog measurement instrument inspired by teenage engineering restraint, NOT retro, not steampunk, not gold jewelry. Front orthographic view, no phones, no hands, no perspective.

Each screen is a slim premium champagne silver panel, fine sandblasted texture, one delicate inset ivory glass display, small CLEAN TUNER header and one tiny settings icon. At bottom a discreet Chromatic selector and A4 440 Hz calibration label. Listening is a tiny status dot and text, NEVER a button. No other large buttons. Very high-end warm material feel but visually calm, clean precision typography, charcoal ink, muted amber luminous details. Compact intentional layout, no empty giant lower halves.

Main display: a SINGLE thin upward arch (like a rainbow's shape only, NOT its colors), spanning 120 degrees, its apex at 12 o'clock. An elegantly hairline etched curved track with tiny subtle ticks. NOT a thick band, not a horseshoe, not a full circle, not a speedometer. Three note labels immediately outside this arch: left note at 10 o'clock, main note at 12 o'clock, right note at 2 o'clock, all baseline upright. Main center label larger than neighbors. Warm amber light gently washes a limited region along the arch near the detected pitch, brighter in the middle, very soft ends. A sharp slender short radial amber marker crosses the track to identify exact pitch. NO long central needle, NO needle hub. NO giant repeated note name below the arc. Below arc center is a compact signed cents value, with tiny FLAT or IN TUNE. Small octave identification under the central note. Same arch size and placement across all three panels. Fixed direction text below arc ends: LOW left, HIGH right.

Exact states:
LEFT SCREEN: G♯ at upper-left arc end, A at apex, A♯ at upper-right arc end. Small 4 under A. Marker at 10.8 degrees LEFT of apex, visibly left of A but much closer to A than to G♯ (neighbor spacing 60 degrees =100 cents). Light centered on marker, softly illuminating A and nearest neighbors. Center readout '-18 ct', small 'FLAT'. Small frequency '435.4 Hz'.
MIDDLE SCREEN: identical G♯ / A / A♯ label positions and identical arc. Small 4 under A. Marker EXACTLY at apex aligned with A. Amber light subtly concentrated symmetrically at apex. Readout '0 ct', 'IN TUNE', '440.0 Hz'.
RIGHT SCREEN: identical geometry but labels B at upper left, C at apex, C♯ at upper right. Small 5 under C. Marker at apex, aligned with C. Readout '0 ct', 'IN TUNE', '523.3 Hz'.
Above screens on presentation canvas use understated labels '01 / A · FLAT', '02 / A · IN TUNE', '03 / C · IN TUNE'. Under left and middle together caption 'SAME NOTE · ONLY THE MARKER MOVES'. Under right caption 'NEW NOTE · SCALE RECENTERS'. Keep these annotation captions outside app panels. A beautiful production-quality app design study that clearly demonstrates current note centered, actual pitch marker moving left/right, neighboring notes visible. Exact legible type, generous margins. No rainbow colors, green smiley, flashy neon, chunky metal arch, full 12 note wheel, repeated huge A, faux screws, wood, or big listening button.
purpose: Three-state concept, not implemented UI. Same-note scale stays stable; confirmed note changes recenter local scale.
review: Labels and readings correct; image is illustrative, tick geometry is not a calibrated implementation.
